paragraphs: Rabbi Yochanan Chakokaa: beginning of Pesachim, 3b. Tosafot cite Rabbeinu Chananel’s explanation: a scribe, like mechokek. Some say he is named after his town: Arukh, entry chak; in Joshua, section 19, ‘And it went out from there to Chukkok.’ On Pesachim 13a, a man deposited leaven with him, and he came before Rabbi. In Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 1:4:6 (cited here as halakhah 5), a person deposited a sack for Passover with Rabbi Chiyya Rabbah. Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Bun said: it was Yochanan Chakokaya; he asked Rabbi. In the Jerusalem Talmud, HaMafkid: Rabbi Yochanan Chakokaya deposited leaven with Rabbi Chiyya Rabbah, and he asked Rabbi [the questioner is not explicit].
